Endurance training increases the muscle's capacity for aerobic (oxidative) energy production, through more mitochondria, higher oxidative enzyme activity, and better capillary supply. Neither option in the team note matches this: endurance training doesn't make muscle contract faster, and it doesn't increase phosphocreatine breakdown, which is an anaerobic process. The note's answer may be a mistake, so it's worth checking before the team relies on it.
CONFIDENCE: 85
